summary: Grafton County, NH emergency fire lookout near Lincoln; listed as gone, with artifacts reported. Almost nothing else is documented.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone. A hiking list gives NW Hancock Spur as no longer standing, with artifacts; no source describes the site today.

evidence.supports: Hancock Spur is in Grafton County
Hancock Spur near Lincoln named as an emergency lookout example
evidence.quote: Examples would be Currier Mountain near Jefferson Notch and Hancock Spur near Lincoln.

evidence.supports: emergency lookouts set up on strategic points in periods of high fire danger, including areas with hazardous fuels from the 1938 hurricane
evidence.quote: Emergency Lookouts were used on strategic points during periods of high fire danger, such as areas with hazardous fuels from the 1938 Hurricane

evidence.supports: emergency lookouts linked by telephone line to a central dispatcher
evidence.quote: They were connected by telephone lines to a central dispatcher.

evidence.supports: hiking list: NW Hancock Spur, Lincoln/Livermore, no longer standing, artifacts
evidence.quote: NW Hancock Spur - Lincoln/Livermore 4000+ No Longer Standing / Artifacts

corrections.why: The Forest Fire Lookout Association list gives the type of Hancock Spur as Unknown; no source read confirms a tower

notes_for_editor: Almost nothing on the tower itself. The Forest Lookouts Hancock Spur page has only the county, with no date, agency or history. Built date, agency and staffing history are not in any source read, so the story leaves them out. The 'emergency lookout' statement is the White Mountain History article's general description of the category, with Hancock Spur given as an example. The hiking list entry 'NW Hancock Spur' is matched by name and the Lincoln/Livermore area, not by a tower record; the story says it may be the same site. The story calls Hancock Spur a site, not a peak: no source read describes its terrain. Correction proposed for kind (tower to unknown) because FFLA lists the type as Unknown; not applied, a human should decide. Search budget: 2 WebSearch calls; about 3 page reads. No photos found.
